65. Cubicle (x): once lowered, it covered the room as indicated by the presence of the lunette and the holes for the housing for the beams, on the N. On the white background, in correspondence with the plaster recarbonated with the polishing to make the color adhere, you can see the imprints of the horizontal and vertical elements that outlined the frieze and the upper area in the III style scheme.

66. Cubicle (x), wall E with splayed window in the N section: despite the complete fall in colour, the awning mentioned above is distinguished by the scheme of panels separated by narrow compartments crossed by candelabra. 80 N59663
67. Cubicle (x): small traces of colour were preserved in the E section of the S wall where, immediately above the illegible plinth, part of a red vertical band could be seen.
68. Cubicle (x): in the N section of the W wall a thin candelabrum can be seen crossing the panel of the middle area and ending with a large chalice at the frieze.

Cubicle (1), N wall: the plaster tapped to make the successive layers adhere better is a symptom of the careful preparation of the fourth style decoration with the white plinth simply framed in panels and compartments sprayed with red; The middle area, divided into panels and compartments, presents in one of these the faint traces of a monochrome picture with dolphins.
70. Cubicle (1), N wall, central section: detail of the picture with dolphins darting to the left.

73. Cubicle (1), wall E, section S: detail of the geometric black plinth with a circle crossed by a horizontal line, in the centre of the panel.
72. Cubicle (1), wall E, section S: detail of the geometric black plinth with a lozenge crossed by a horizontal line, in the centre of the panel.

74. Cubicle (1), wall O with walled square window. The decoration with a bipartite structure with a white plinth sprinkled with red presented in the central compartment a painting with doors with Narcissus (41x45 cm) seated. The side panels bordered by simple vertical bands and, at the top, by a border of carpet with staples, have panels with cupids in the center.

75. Cubicle (1), wall O, central section: detail of the compartment with the door painting with Narcissus seated on a cubic base, near a body of water and with trees in the background. The crowned young man holds with his right hand in a position of abandonment the skewers and a flap of the red mantle that partially covers his shoulders.

76. Cubicle (1), O wall, S section: from the faint traces that remain, it is clear why the group of Eros and Psyche had been defined by Mau as "graceful and new in composition and movement" (RM 1898, p. 21). In fact, Psyche's body is completely hidden behind Eros, only the wings and the face that she approaches that of her beloved protrude.
77. Cubicle (1), wall O, section E: detail of the upper part of the middle area with the edge of a stapled carpet surmounted by a square.
1. Vestibule (a): threshold formed by two limestone slabs with recesses for hinges and bolts.

2. Atrium (b): view from the east of the atrium transformed from Tuscan to tetrastyle with the addition of brick columns around the small impluvium, belonging to the oldest layout as well as the beautiful travertine table, under which there were two small cylindrical altars, one of travertine, the other of alabaster. 80 N59748

3. Atrium (b): impluvium covered with earthenware with sparse white scales, now very worn, from which the water flowed directly into the street, through underground pipes, since there was no cistern. 80 N59751

4. Atrium (b), N wall against which the end of a masonry staircase, now disappeared, leans. The hoof and the middle area are completely discolored. The terracotta pillar was found in the impluvium where, covered by a slab, it served as an altar.

5. Atrium (b): detail of one of the supports of the travertine table decorated on the front face with a lion's paw, stylized in grooves and scales at the top and ending laterally in an acanthus volute with bellflower bud at the top and semi-palmette at the bottom. It is an elegant work of Hellenistic tradition referable to the second century BC.

6. Cubicle (d): the N wall, like the opposite S wall, had a bipartite structure with a yellow plinth, a white middle area with an architectural foreshortening in the center, crossed by twisted candelabra and side panels with vignettes of metal vases
7. Cubicle (d), wall E, with two splayed windows and large quadrangular holes for the support beams of the floor above. The plinth is completely illegible; the white midfield exhibitsINS. 15, 6
8. Cubicle(s): cocciopesto floor. 80 N58742
9. Cubicle (e): nothing more can be distinguished than the original decorative partition on wall E of this room, with a white background.
11. Corridor (g): the N wall retains, in the middle area, residues of the black panel decoration with large yellow borders.

10. 'Tablino (f): the almost total fall of the painted plaster, with the exception of a small residue on a yellow background in the middle area, has highlighted the preparation substrate tapped to make the most superficial layers of the unfinished decoration adhere better. The back wall, closed after the earthquake of 62 AD, had no cladding.
12. Corridor (k): in section O there are remains of the cocciopesto floor with white limestone flakes.

13. Corridor (k): wall O retains the original decoration pertaining to the single large living room (1). The black geometric plinth is separated from the middle area by a thin white band with scrolled motifs; the middle area, also black, was divided into panels and in the central one there was the painting with Heracles and Omphale, of which only the lower part now remains; in the side panels, as can be recognized from the opposite wall E, there were vignettes. 80 N59735
14. Triclinium (1): the floor is made of cocciopesto with sparse flakes of limestone.  80 N59734

15. Triclinium (1): the N wall has a refined decoration of the fourth style interrupted by the quadrangular window obtained later in the upper part. At the bottom, the wall is not perpendicular to the floor but oblique to obtain more space for triclinary beds. The black plinth is divided into panels and compartments with geometric elements; the middle area, also black, has an aedicule with a picture in the center and panels with vignettes separated by narrow compartments with candelabra that continue to the upper area. In the frieze there are still life paintings separated by metal candelabra. The area
16. 'Triclinium (1), N wall: detail of section O with recess for triclinium beds. 80 N59707

Triclinium (1), wall N: panel E of the plinth has a geometric scheme with a medallion and two hemimedallions connected by orthogonal and oblique lines with a narrow globe compartment has a rectangle with short concave sides, containing opposing buds, connected vertically to two small rectangles.

19. Triclinium (1), N wall, section O with the extreme half-panel, on a black background, crossed by an edge of scrolled carpet and part of the central aedicule with the column interrupted by purple bands with golden studs. The black frieze, above the dentilled cornice, is crossed by a short metal candelabrum to which the arched garlands are connected.

20. Triclinium (1), N wall: painting with a scene of uncertain interpretation; perhaps a little-known myth of Artemis if it is identified with the goddess la. female figure judging by her clothing: the short tunic, the high hunter's shoes, the quiver on the right shoulder; and by the attributes of the cupid that rests on her legs such as the bow and the radiated crown that she wears on her head. Problematic is the identification of the young man with an athletic appearance, with spit, sword and quiver, then a hunter, covered only around the legs by the purple mantle, and almost subjugated by the resourcefulness of the goddess who touches his chin with her right hand as if to raise his face. It is precisely the attitude of the female figure, unusual for Artemis, unless one thinks of a variant of the myth of Hippolytus (Robert), that has led some authors to see Atalanta with Meleager (Rumpf) or Meilanion (Herbig), others Dido with Aeneas (Sogliano and Rumpf), others Aphrodite with Adonis (Schefold). 21. Triclinium (1), N wall: narrow black panels with a vignette of cupids in flight, bordered vertically by the edges of a scrolled carpet and separated by a compartment crossed by a gilded twisted candelabrum, characterize the middle area to the right of the painting.

23. Triclinium (1), N wall, section E: detail of the right panel with the vignette of a cupid in flight holding in front of him, at chest height, a alabastron (?). The presence of color makes the graffiti contour line even more evident, also present in the other panel.
22. Triclinium (1), N wall, section E: detail of the left panel with a vignette of a cupid in flight with indistinguishable attributes.

24. Triclinium (1), N wall: the upper area is interrupted on the left by the presence of the window, so the epistyle of the aedicule is incomplete. In the right section there is the frieze with pictures of still lifes and short metal candelabra between a lower frame with dentils and an upper one with ovals on which rest two aedicules with Apollonian elements such as acroteria and a long twisted gilded candelabrum supporting a small picture with a mask. A band with stylized lotus bud motifs and a molded stucco frame crown the end of the wall.
25. Triclinium (1), N wall, section E: detail of the epistyle of the central aedicule with ovoli frame and acroterial volute.
26. Triclinium (1), N wall: left section of the frieze with a still life picture (a tray and an overturned basket?).

27. Triclinium (1), N wall: central section of the frieze with the short metal candelabra with lion's paws to which the arched garlands and the gilded twisted candelabrum are connected which, starting in the middle area and ending in the upper one, is placed in front of the dentilled and ovule cornices that delimit the frieze.
28. Triclinium (1), N wall: right section of the frieze with a picture of a still life (dead bird?) completely illegible, unlike the very well preserved dentilled and ovule frames.

30. Triclinium (1), N wall, section E: detail of the gilded twisted candelabrum that crosses the upper area and ends with a disk, only half depicted, below the white band with stylized lotus buds. A small box picture hangs from the shaft, with a mask.

29. Triclinium (1), N wall, section E: detail of the left aedicule in the upper area. The structure, seen in a slight glimpse from the left, has a coffered ceiling from which a basket is suspended; A lyra and a griffin facing right act as acroteri.
31. Triclinium (1), N wall, section E: detail of the box picture with swan-neck side walls, containing a comic mask. 80 N59713

32. Triclinium (1), N wall, section E: detail of the aedicule at the E end and seen in a slight foreshortening from the right, with a coffered ceiling from which a rhytòn is suspended. A griffin facing left, a lyra and a swan act as acroteria. 80 N59709

33. Triclinium (1), N wall, section E: detail of the epistyle of the aedicule with acroterial griffin, lyra and swan, explicit Apollonian symbols consistent with the themes dealt with in the paintings on the N and E walls related to Artemis.

34. Triclinium (1), wall E: there was the same scheme as the N wall with a black geometric plinth, a black middle area with a painting in the central aedicule and vignettes in the side panels, bordered by square carpet edges. Only a short stretch remains of the frieze and the upper area, probably similar to that of the other wall, although with variations in the details.
35. Triclinium (1), wall E, section N: detail of the frieze with another explicit Apollonian element such as the Delphic tripod, next to the completely lost picture.

36. Triclinium (1), wall E, section N: detail of the black geometric plinth with a panel divided into four quadrants, each of which is divided into two parts, by a thyrsus placed diagonally connected to the central rectangle. The inward inclination of the N wall at the triclinium bed is evident.

37. Triclinium (1), wall E, central section: detail of the painting, found only in the lower left half and now completely lost, with Artemis and Zeus. The goddess, with radiated crown, quiver and bow was depicted standing near the throne of Zeus.

38. Triclinium (1): in front of the W wall, of which only the black background color is recognizable, there is a fluted terracotta cistern mouth with triglyphs to adorn the band below the edge, datable to the second century BC.  80 N59731
39. Triclinium (1): in the same place there is also a sima of the valley with a lion's head drip between palmettes.   80 N59732
40. Courtyard (m), E wall with amphorae necks and quadrangular niche.
41. Courtyard (m), S wall covered with rough plaster, with a square triclinium window (1). 80 N59747 V.S.

1. Façade of the house with the entrances at nos. 7 and 8, by N. The N half, preserved for a maximum height of 6.20 m, shows under the plaster of the years immediately preceding 79 A.D. an opus incertum of the late second century B.C. The S half was renovated into opus reticulatum in the Augusteotibian era. The row of beam holes for a canopy was completed in an S-shape in modern times.

2. Fauces(b), Scon wall decoration in simple IV style. Among the black fields of the middle zone is a candelabra. The upper area is in fake opus quadratum. Next to the pillar, on the atrium side, is a hole on both sides. At night there was a reinforcement beam inserted in the leaves of the closed door.

3. : Atrium (d), view towards the E, on the fauces (b) and, to the N of them, on the servile cubicle (a) with three stone steps of a staircase that was otherwise wooden that led from the atrium (d) to an intermediate floor (pergula) and to the second floor above (a)-(c). DAIB 75.2.098
4. Atrium (d), corner S-E with cubicle entrance (c). DAIB 75.2.099

5. Atrium (d), wall N: as far as the painting is preserved, 5.70 m high, the wall is original. Very simple fourth-style decorative scheme with black plinth, red middle area with simple profiled fields, with vignettes with birds and upper area with rows of ashlars.

6. Atrium (d), section S: on the left, doorway on the cubicle (c), in the centre, passage to the portico (1), on the right, opening on the tablinum (e)) (width 3.49 m) with marble threshold. In the foreground impluvium and marble table. The original portions of the S wall and their paintings are preserved for a maximum height of 4.90 m.  DAIB 80.3.300

7. Atrium (d), section O: on the left the passage to the portico (l), in the background, moved towards the S, the tablinum (e) with passage to the cubicle (f). Both have a window overlooking the garden (n). On the right, kitchen door (g). Both the architrave, 2.96 m high from the threshold level, and the masonry above it are modern. The wall above the kitchen door is original up to a height of 4.91 m, but the lintel is modern.   DAIB 80.3.425
8. Marble table (cartibulum) in the atrium (d). External side of the support plate No. Approximately 50 A.D.
9. Marble table (cartibulum) in the atrium (d). Outer side of the support slab S. About 50 A.D.

10. Cubicle (c), wall E: the dentilled cornice and the upper area with the marginal cornice interrupted by the window are of the first style (about 100 BC); the paintings of the plinth and the middle area, each with a swan or goat as a vignette of the field, reveal a very simple scheme of the early IV style. On the N and S walls, and in the upper area of the E wall, there are repairs in rough plaster following the earthquake of 62 AD.

11. Cubicle (c): view through the atrium on the tablinum (e). The plinth and middle area are of the fourth style, the dentilled frame of the first style. At 3.56 m in height is the impost of the reconstructed segment vault, on the E-W axis. DAIB 78.2.308

12. Tablinum (e), wall O with passage to the cubicle (f). The impost of the segmented vault, once oriented on the EO axis, is 3.15 m from the floor level. The sober decoration of the fourth style consists of a black plinth and two fields with a white background with pinax (a vase) above the door frame. Between them is a simple architectural glimpse. Dolphins and a hippocampus float in the lunette.
13. Tablinum (e): pinax (18 x 35 cm) on wall O: still life with marine animals, IV style.
14. Tablinum (e), wall N: decoration of the fourth style, corresponding to that of wall O.
15. Tablinum (e), wall N: pinax on the right (18 x 35 cm) with hunting scenes on a dark red background. IV style.

17. Cubicle (f), wall S: the room, which receives a lot of light thanks to a large window overlooking the garden, and an oculus, was used as a bedroom and living room by the owner and his lady. The stucco cornice above the middle area is pertinent to the earlier decoration in the third style and was preserved even in later times.

16. Cubicle (f), N wall: above the black plinth, the middle area with a white background is divided by red bands into two fields, between which is a pilaster with a marsh cane candelabrum. The vignettes of the fields consist of two roe deer facing each other. IV style. The stucco frame of the lunette belongs to the remains of an older decoration in the third style.

18. In the N-W corner of the kitchen (g) there is the masonry hearth; in the N wall, above it, is the niche for a second lararium. On the right you can see the marked slope of the floor in the direction of the latrine.

19. Porch (1), N wall with passage to the atrium (d); the original masonry is preserved up to the height of the modern sloping roof. The upper margin of the decoration in the fourth style indicates that the original roof was flat and that above it was a room on the second floor. DAIB 78.3.331
20. Porch (1): pinax (20x 46 cm) of the N wall: two birds and fruits, IV style.

21. Porch (1), wall E: passage and window on the workshop (i), on the right the jamb N of the triclinium (k). In the background, entrance from no. 7 on the stairwell (p). Next to this, the exit from the room (i) to the exterior, walled up after the 62

22. Triclinium (k), wall E: the decoration of the main representative room of the house is relatively sumptuous. Above the dark red plinth, richly decorated, is the middle area with a white background divided by candelabra-aedicules into three fields, framed by large perforated borders. The central field, with a figured central square, is further highlighted by an elaborate decorative structure. In the side camps they are floating cupids. The candelabra are extended in the

23. Triclinium (k), wall N: the decoration, preserved in a fairly satisfactory state, varies the scheme of wall E almost motif by motif, but does not differ from it in the general impression of mostly flat, but irrational and heavy splendour. IV initial style (50-60 AD).

24. Triclinium (k), S wall: originally the decoration corresponded exactly to that of the N wall. Evidently the earthquake of 62 AD seriously damaged this wall, so the masonry had to undergo repairs and the gaps created in the fresco were temporarily filled with rough plaster.

25. Triclinium (k), central picture (56 x 55 cm) on the N wall: Perseus shows Andromeda liberated the reflected image of Medusa's severed head. The theme is known in Pompeian mural painting in no less than twelve other variations.

26. Triclinium (k), central picture (55 x 53.5 cm) on the S wall: Adonis (on the left, with cloak and spear) does not allow himself to be distracted by Venus (on the right, with his arm raised) and Cupid from undertaking the fatal hunt.
27. Triclinium (k), N wall: detail of the upper area with Bacchus' panther and goat, nibbling grapes. Diap. DAIB (Fot. P. Grunwald)
28. Triclinium (k), wall E, detail of the upper area: two griffins with garlands do not let themselves be disturbed by two jumping goats.

29. View towards the S through the portico (1) on the summer exedra (m), built at a later time. On the left, the window of the room (i), then the large entrance to the triclinium (k). The architrave of the exedra and the overhanging masonry are modern.
30. Esedra (m), S wall: the room is only 2.70 m wide and 1.70 m deep, and was specially built to contain a single, spacious sofa for summer nights. Rich decoration fills the area
31. Exedra (m), S wall: detail of the central picture depicting Bacchus (height 90 cm) resting his left hand on the thyrsus and with his right empty of a kàntharos the wine, licked by a panther.

33. Exedra (m), wall W: detail of fig. previous.

Exedra (m), wall E: the composition corresponds in detail to that of wall O, however, due to the presence in the central field of a small window (32 x 40 cm) with oblique jambs oriented towards the lararium, to allow the gods of the house to protect the apotheca (0), the large figures represented on the S and W walls are missing.  the remaining surface of which is empty. IV initial style (50-60 AD). DAIB 75.2.156
35. Exedra (m), wall E: pinax (19.5 x 33 cm) with two cupids handling jewels and the mirror of Venus. IV initial style (50-60 AD). Diap. DAIB (Fot. P. Grunwald)
36. Exedra (m), wall E, detail: the goat on the pierced border takes up a motif from the triclinium (k), decorated by the same craftsman who worked in the exedra (m). Diap. DAIB (Fot. Grunwald)

37. Exedra (m), S wall, detail: in a boldly contracted architecture it is a finax with landscape: three figures cross a bridge over a greenish river. In the background there is a sacred area with votive columns and a temple in yellow ochre with black-brown shades, in the background a pavilion with columns in blue-gray.
38. Exedra (m), S wall, detail: the frontal peacock is one of the typical motifs that express the splendour dear to the IV style.

39. On the west wall of the garden (n) is the lararium (height 2.75 m) built in the shape of a temple. It is pertinent to the layout in the fourth style of the 50s of the first century AD; it was repaired following the earthquake of 62 AD.

40. Garden (n), lararium, detail: the internal stucco columns are red, the external yellow. The capitals have a dark red kàlathos and blue acanthus leaves. On the yellow attic rests a blue pediment, interrupted by an arch above the central intercolumnium. All the cornices and the archivolt have ornamental strips typical of the IV style, in stucco in painted relief.

41. The Lares guardians of the house: the lararium in the garden (n) was designed in such a way that the gods of the house could look through windows and doors at all the rooms of the house. The three rooms (c), (g), (h) that did not fall within their field of vision were protected by a second lararium located in the kitchen (g). In the fauces, which were not included in the lararium's protective radius, there are indications of the presence of a specific guardian deity. Drawing by M. Sohn
42. Garden (n), section N: on the left is the lararium, at the bottom left the cubicle window (f), on the right the tablinum window (e).
43. Garden (n), section S: in the right half of the wall + $ you can recognize the remains of a limestone frame masonry. On the left, the window of the exedra (m).
44. Terracotta puteale dicisterna in the N-E corner of the garden (n). Late Republican-Augustan era.

46. Figure of the marble table support in the garden (n). A bearded and bald Silenus lovingly holds Bacchus as a child wrapped in a cloth with both arms. Above the loincloth protrudes his bare belly. Valuable work of the late Augustan period.

45. Marble table in the garden (n), now in the Antiquarium of Pompeii (height 102.5 cm; slab: 69.2 x 45 cm). From a lion's foot, fixed to a dark gray marble base and crowned with scrolls of acanthus leaves, rise the table supports, slightly curved and flared upwards; in front of them is the bust of a Silenus with a child Bacchus in his arms. DAIB 83.2.237

1. Cubicle(s): cocciopesto floor with the field characterized by small black and white flakes scattered and the carpet made up of a network of diamonds. Two rhomboidal tiles of white and gray marble seem to belong to a previous arrangement.
3. Cubicle (a), N wall: detail of the frieze with stucco pilasters and a floor pertaining to the cornice above. 80 N56813

2. Cubicle (a): the N wall, like the others, has been redecorated in the fourth style in the lower part with white panels squared in red and retains the upper area of the original first style covering with a frieze of stucco pilasters imagined as a pillared gallery.

4. Cubicle (a): the E wall with a quadrangular window, also retains the white plinth with plants, as well as the middle area of the IV style; of the previous first style remains part of the frieze with stucco pilasters.
5. Cubicle (a): the O wall, with the door to the atrium, also had two windows, of which the right one was closed.

6. Vestibule (b): sparse pisatrelle and flakes of polychrome marble are bedded in the papier-mâché floor, according to a technique in use in the second century BC. On the N wall, covered with rough plaster, a niche of arched lararium is edged and covered inside with white plaster.
7. Vestibule (b), wall N: detail of the lararium niche with white plaster cladding.

8. Cubicle (c): also in this room there remain, in the upper part, conspicuous remains of the primitive decoration of the first style with the stucco frame with dentils, the white plaster frieze and the floor pertaining to a molded stucco frame

9. Cubicle (c), wall E with splayed window at the top. The hoof and midfield appear to be coated. of simple white plaster, while the dentilled cornice and the rough frieze crowned at the top by a molded stucco frame and the lunette with a red background, belong to the decoration of the first style.
10. Cubicle (c), wall E: detail of the moulded stucco frame and the lunette with a red background above which the holes for the support beams of the false ceiling can be seen.
11. Cubicle (c), S wall: the stucco dentilled cornice, the rough plaster frieze above and the moulded stucco cornice are fairly well preserved in section E.
12. Atrium (d): taken from the N that allows you to see the impluvium, the valley and the wooden staircase for the mezzanine.
13. Atrium(d): the floor and the bottom of the impluvium have the same cocciopesto covering with scattered polychrome marble flakes and tiles. The tub is painted in yellow, red and purple.

14. Atrium (d): to the W of the impluvium there is, embedded in the cocciopesto floor built above a pre-existing one, a cistern mouth (height 58 cm, diameter 51 cm) of fluted travertine, whose mouth is very worn.
15. Ala(s): cocciopesto floor with scattered marble chips.

16. Wing (e): view from the S of the room as a whole with the cocciopesto floor and the walls covered with a high black plinth and with a middle and upper area of simple rough plaster. The holes for the beams suggest the presence of a sturdy walkable slab.
17. Triclinium (f): marble threshold for a door with three leaves, one of which is fixed, with recesses for hinges and bolts.

18. Triclinium (f): cocciopesto floor with a carpet consisting of rows of crosses with a black central tile, bordered by a row of white tiles placed side by side; the marginal flounce has small flakes of scattered polychrome limestone.

19. Triclinium (f), N wall: the white plinth (?), now illegible, was divided into panels and compartments; in the middle area the panels can be distinguished, bordered by edges of palmette carpet or taut garlands and separated from each other by narrow compartments crossed by gilded candelabras. In the middle of each of the central panels was a vignette (bird, quadruped, pair of dolphins).
20. In the triclinium (f) are deposited part of the stone materials, mostly drums of columns, capitals and tuff blocks, coming from the tests carried out by A. Maiuri near the northern walls.
21. In the small latrine of the room (h) the downpipe of clay pipes ended. The holes for housing beams on the O wall and the recess on the N wall denote the presence of an upper mezzanine. 80 N56802
1. View from the outside of the thermopolium with the masonry counter in room (b), also accessible from number 15.
2. Thermopolium (b): the counter with dolii embedded in the marble-covered shelf and ladder for the display of food leaning against the S wall.

3. Corridor (c): the S wall, more than the N wall, preserves remains of the IV style decoration with a yellow plinth divided into panels and compartments and a median area, also yellow, with panels bordered by triangle carpet edges.

4. Workshop (e) located to the S of the corridor (c). In the threshold, in three blocks of trachyte, the groove for the portcullis and the recesses for the hinges of the small passage door, on the right, are visible.

5. Atrium (f), wall S, section between the doors of the rooms (m) and (n): on the yellow plinth there is the red panel of the middle area with the edges of a semicircular carpet and the imprint of the covering of wooden boards on which a painting (53x45.5 cm) was perhaps mounted.

6. Atrium (f), wall O: in the red middle area, with panels with carpet edges completely similar to those of wall S, the separation compartment between the different panels is also preserved. The imprint of the wooden plank cladding (91x71 cm) is much larger than that on the S wall.
7. Tablinum (h): of the floor covering only a few elements remain of the central emblem with stars formed by hexagons of bardiglio and triangles of palombino.
8. Tablinum (h): the border of the emblem in opus sectile with gray hexagonal tiles and white trian-olar was made up of gray marble rods.

123. Exedra (G), wall E, central panel (width 1.17 m), damaged in the upper part: Jason in front of Pelias. The scene of sacrifice is divided into three groups.
